missions.fullAnalysis: Strategic focus: Nominative subject. 'День' stays in the nominative case as the subject. 'Хороший' is the agreeing masculine adjective, and 'сегодня' sets the time frame.
Strategic focus: Accusative object. As an inanimate masculine noun, 'день' is identical in the accusative, here the object of 'жду'. 'Этот' agrees in the masculine.
Strategic focus: Genitive of relation. 'Дня' is genitive after 'конца', and the fleeting 'е' drops out of the stem. The whole phrase follows 'до', also a genitive preposition.
Strategic focus: Dative of direction. 'Дню' is the dative after 'к', with the fleeting vowel dropped. 'Этому' agrees in the masculine dative.
Strategic focus: Instrumental of time. 'Днём' is the instrumental form used adverbially to mean during the day. A very common time expression in Russian.
Strategic focus: Prepositional case. 'О дне' uses the prepositional after 'о' to mark the topic, keeping the fleeting vowel. 'Прошлом' agrees in the masculine prepositional.
Strategic focus: Genitive after 'после'. 'Дня' is genitive following 'после', with the fleeting vowel dropped. 'Дождливого' agrees, and 'солнце' is the nominative subject.
Strategic focus: Genitive plural after a number. 'Дней' is the genitive plural required after 'семь'. 'В неделе' is prepositional, marking the timespan.
Strategic focus: Nominative plural. 'Дни' is the nominative plural subject of 'были'. 'Эти' agrees, and 'тёплыми' is the instrumental plural predicate adjective.
Strategic focus: Accusative plural with 'за'. 'Дни' is the accusative plural after 'за' in a time span. 'Последние' agrees, and 'погода' is the nominative subject.
